newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE-100 set for quiet consolidation.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE-100 set for quiet consolidation.

text.p: The FTSE 100 share index visited record heights last week but consolidation is on the cards for this week, technical analysts said on Monday. "The outlook for this week is neutral or slightly bearish... 4,020 was broken and the bull run from the start of July has definitely weakened," Julius de Kempanaer, analyst at the Institute for Research & Investment Services in Rotterdam, said.

"Negative divergence on the relative strength indicator has built up over the last two months, pointing to sideways to corrective action while the 10-day moving average was crossed on the downside," he said.
The FTSE 100 last week touched an all-time high of 4,073.2 points early in the week but dipped below 4,000 mid-week.
De Kempanaer said the market was unlikely to climb back to its all-time highs in the next couple of weeks, a view echoed by David Sneddon, technical analyst at Credit Suisse in London.
"We're more likely to consolidate this week or the next two weeks and could even see correction before the uptrend resumes. We won't be revisiting the highs," Sneddon said.
While de Kempanaer saw the market neutral or slightly weaker, Sneddon said the FTSE had scope to push up to soft resistance at 4,029 points and then edge further up.
"Then we're looking at possibly a move on to 4,035 or 4,040 before coming under pressure...I'm neutral to bullish for today but don't see anything hugely dramatic," Sneddon said.
But both agreed the market could slide sharply if the FTSE broke what they described as critical support at 3,980 points. Initial support was pegged at 4,017 and 4,000 by Sneddon.
"If 3,980 were broken, then this market could head down to 3,900 points..but we're not in for a crash," de Kempanaer said.
